extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts reporting animal experiments (preclinical/in vivo researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist for authors to ensure complete, transparent reporting of in vivo (animal) experiments following the ARRIVE 2.0 guidance. Covers an Essential 10 minimum items plus a Recommended Set of contextual items to allow assessment of reliability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment, provide brief details of study design including the groups being compared, including control groups. If no control group has been used, the rationale should be stated. Specify the experimental unit (e.g. a single animal, litter, or cage of animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These details should make clear what comparisons were made and the unit of analysis so readers and reviewers can interpret results and replication attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Specify the exact number of experimental units allocated to each group, and the total number in each experiment, and indicate the total number of animals used. b. Explain how the sample size was decided, providing details of any a priori sample size calculation, if done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both per-group and overall counts and any power or sample-size calculations used to justify group sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Describe any criteria used for including and excluding animals (or experimental units) during the experiment, and data points during the analysis, and specify if these criteria were established a priori. b. For each experimental group, report any animals, experimental units or data points not included in the analysis and explain why. c. For each analysis, report the exact value of n in each experimental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about prespecified vs post-hoc exclusions and fully report exclusions and per-analysis sample sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: a. State whether randomisation was used to allocate experimental units to control and treatment groups and, if done, provide the method used to generate the randomisation sequence. b. Describe the strategy used to minimise potential confounders such as the order of treatments and measurements, or animal/cage location. If confounders were not controlled, state this explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include method details (e.g., random number generator, blocking) and describe any steps to reduce systematic bias from order/location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe who was aware of the group allocation at the different stages of the experiment (during the allocation, the conduct of the experiment, the outcome assessment, and the data analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report who was blinded and at which stages; if blinding was not possible, state this and describe any mitigation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Clearly define all outcome measures assessed (e.g. cell death, molecular markers, or behavioural changes). b. For hypothesis-testing studies, specify the primary outcome measure, i.e. the outcome measure that was used to determine the sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish primary vs secondary outcomes and give operational definitions so outcomes are unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Provide details of the statistical methods used for each analysis, including software used. b. Describe any methods used to assess whether the data met the assumptions of the statistical approach, and what was done if the assumptions were not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State specific tests/models, handling of multiple comparisons, transformation or non-parametric alternatives, and software (with versions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Provide species-appropriate details of the animals used, including species, strain and substrain, sex, age or developmental stage, and, if relevant, weight. b. Provide further relevant information on the provenance of animals, health/immune status, genetic modification status, genotype, and any previous procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply details necessary to interpret biological variability and replicate the model (source, genotype, health status, prior manipulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experimental group, including controls, describe the procedures in enough detail to allow others to replicate them, including: a. What was done, how it was done and what was used. b. When and how often. c. Where (including detail of any acclimatisation periods). d. Why (provide rationale for procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide procedural detail (materials, doses, timings, settings, acclimatisation) and rationale to enable reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results (descriptive statistics and effect sizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment conducted, including independent replications, report: a. Summary/descriptive statistics for each experimental group, with a measure of variability where applicable (e.g. mean and SD, or median and range). b. If applicable, the effect size with a confidence interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report per-group summaries, variability measures, and effect sizes with CIs to facilitate interpretation of magnitude and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an accurate summary of the research objectives, animal species, strain and sex, key methods, principal findings, and study conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the abstract contains the key elements of the study and animal model so readers quickly understand scope and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Include sufficient scientific background to understand the rationale and context for the study, and explain the experimental approach. b. Explain how the animal species and model used address the scientific objectives and, where appropriate, the relevance to human biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contextual justification for model choice and link to broader literature and translational relevance where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly describe the research question, research objectives and, where appropriate, specific hypotheses being tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear, testable objectives and hypotheses to frame study design and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the name of the ethical review committee or equivalent that has approved the use of animals in this study, and any relevant licence or protocol numbers (if applicable). If ethical approval was not sought or granted, provide a justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include approval body and identifiers or an explicit justification when approval was not obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of housing and husbandry conditions, including any environmental enrichment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report housing (cage type, bedding), group vs single housing, light/dark cycle, temperature/humidity, and enrichment to contextualise animal welfare influences on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Describe any interventions or steps taken in the experimental protocols to reduce pain, suffering and distress. b. Report any expected or unexpected adverse events. c. Describe the humane endpoints established for the study, the signs that were monitored and the frequency of monitoring. If the study did not have humane endpoints, state this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail analgesia, welfare monitoring, adverse events, and endpoint criteria to demonstrate ethical conduct and allow appraisal of animal welfare influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation / scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Interpret the results, taking into account the study objectives and hypotheses, current theory and other relevant studies in the literature. b. Comment on the study limitations including potential sources of bias, limitations of the animal model, and imprecision associated with the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss findings in context, acknowledge limitations and biases, and avoid overstating conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability / translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on whether, and how, the findings of this study are likely to generalise to other species or experimental conditions, including any relevance to human biology (where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address external validity and limits on translation to other models or humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement indicating whether a protocol (including the research question, key design features, and analysis plan) was prepared before the study, and if and where this protocol was registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State prospective registration or provide explanation if not registered; include registry identifiers where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement describing if and where study data are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify repositories, access conditions, and any persistent identifiers for datasets to support reproducibility and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Declare any potential conflicts of interest, including financial and non-financial. If none exist, this should be stated. b. List all funding sources (including grant identifier) and the role of the funder(s) in the design, analysis and reporting of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose conflicts and provide full funding details including funder roles to allow assessment of potential biases.
